---
id: cpp-merge-slots
title: Merge Charging Slots
difficulty: Medium
order: 1
tags: vector, sort, intervals, in-place
---
## Statement
A charging station logs `n` reserved time intervals `[s, e)` (half-open, `s < e`) in arbitrary order. Merge all overlapping **or touching** intervals (`[1,3)` and `[3,5)` become `[1,5)`), then print:

1. the merged intervals in increasing order, one per line as `s e`,
2. `busy T`: the total covered time,
3. `longest_gap G`: the longest free gap between consecutive merged intervals (0 if there's only one).

n is up to 300 000 and times fit in `long long`. Use a `std::vector`, sort once, and merge **in place** (no second vector needed).

## Starter
```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

int main() {
    std::ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n;
    std::cin >> n;
    std::vector<std::pair<long long, long long>> v(n);
    for (auto& [s, e] : v) std::cin >> s >> e;
}
```

## Hints
- `std::sort` on `pair`s orders by start, then end.
- Keep a write index `w`. For each interval, if it starts at or before `v[w].second`, extend `v[w].second = max(...)`; otherwise copy it to `v[++w]`. Finally `v.resize(w + 1)`.
- Use `'\n'` instead of `std::endl` when printing 300 000 lines, since `endl` flushes every time.

## Solution
```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>

int main() {
    std::ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    std::cin.tie(nullptr);
    int n;
    std::cin >> n;
    std::vector<std::pair<long long, long long>> v(n);
    for (auto& [s, e] : v) std::cin >> s >> e;

    std::sort(v.begin(), v.end());
    std::size_t w = 0;
    for (std::size_t i = 1; i < v.size(); ++i) {
        if (v[i].first <= v[w].second) v[w].second = std::max(v[w].second, v[i].second);
        else v[++w] = v[i];
    }
    v.resize(w + 1);

    long long busy = 0, gap = 0;
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < v.size(); ++i) {
        std::cout << v[i].first << ' ' << v[i].second << '\n';
        busy += v[i].second - v[i].first;
        if (i) gap = std::max(gap, v[i].first - v[i - 1].second);
    }
    std::cout << "busy " << busy << "\nlongest_gap " << gap << '\n';
}
```

Sorting by start makes overlaps adjacent, so one linear pass merges everything: O(n log n) overall. The in-place merge with a write index is the vector equivalent of the remove-erase idiom. It compacts the kept elements to the front, then `resize` drops the tail. That gives no extra allocation, and the data stays contiguous and cache-friendly. `sync_with_stdio(false)` plus `cin.tie(nullptr)` makes iostreams fast enough for large inputs.
